podcast.body: Released in 1999, this album is considered "the high water mark for pop punk." Its cover controversially featured porn star Janine Lindemolder posing as a "naughty nurse." The album's lyrical themes ranged widely, from romantic frustration and Ramones-style pop to the existence of aliens and, notably, "team suicide" (as in the song "Adam Song"), which was presented sympathetically. The album, which embraced a spirit of "goofiness and fun," sold over 15 million copies worldwide. "But then in 1999, they released their Enema of the State album. This represented the high water mark for pop punk."

The original album title was "Turn Your Head and Cough," but photographer Dave Goldman's idea for the glove inspired the band to change the title to its final version. "That's a pretty sexy nurse in the cover of Blink 182's 1999 album, Enema of the State."

podcast.body: This album, originally conceived as "Turn Your Head and Cough," began recording in January 1999 and continued for three months at various California studios, produced by Jerry Finn. It achieved global sales exceeding 15 million copies, largely propelled by hit singles like "What's My Age Again?", "All the Small Things," and "Adam's Song." The album cemented the band's success during a time when pop punk had become very popular with fans. "Nursery rhymes on steroids.
